description: We are RunTime in Space, a team passionate about space exploration, AI, and technology. We are building AstroHealth, a web-based system to monitor astronauts' health using AI and data analysis. We welcome members interested in AI/ML, Python, Data Science, Web Development, UI/UX, Healthcare, and Space Science. Join us to turn ideas into solutions and contribute to the future of space exploration!
summary:
AstroHealth is a web-based health monitoring and decision-support application designed to help astronauts monitor their health during long-duration space missions, where access to immediate medical assistance may be limited.

The platform combines wearable-style vital-sign monitoring, daily manual health check-ins, and photo-based skin and wound assessments in a unified dashboard. It uses transparent, predefined health thresholds to classify readings, alongside trend forecasting and an LSTM-based anomaly detection model to identify unusual heart-rate patterns. When urgent situations arise, astronauts can access 11 predefined emergency medical protocols that operate fully offline.

Additionally, AstroHealth features an AI-powered medical assistant that retrieves information from NASA medical and human-spaceflight resources, providing answers with traceable source references.

By transforming health data into understandable status indicators, early warnings, and actionable guidance, AstroHealth aims to support astronaut self-monitoring and medical decision-making during missions where communication delays and limited medical resources create additional challenges.
details:
1. Project Overview

AstroHealth is a web-based health monitoring and decision-support platform designed to support astronauts during long-duration space missions.

Space missions expose astronauts to multiple health risks, while distance from Earth, communication delays, and limited access to medical professionals make continuous health monitoring and timely assistance essential.

AstroHealth brings health monitoring, data analysis, anomaly detection, emergency guidance, and AI-powered medical information retrieval together in one platform. It aims to help astronauts understand their health status, identify unusual patterns, and access structured guidance when needed.

The system is designed as an integrated prototype that combines traditional rule-based monitoring with machine learning and AI-powered assistance.

2. Problem & Motivation

Astronauts face unique health challenges during long-duration space missions. NASA identifies five major hazards of human spaceflight: space radiation, isolation and confinement, distance from Earth, altered gravity, and the hostile or closed environment.

These conditions can affect astronauts' physical and psychological health. At the same time, communication delays and limited access to medical professionals make immediate medical support more challenging.

Traditional health monitoring alone may not be sufficient to provide a unified view of an astronaut's health, identify unusual patterns over time, and offer accessible guidance during emergencies.

AstroHealth addresses this challenge by bringing health monitoring, data analysis, anomaly detection, emergency protocols, and medical information retrieval into one integrated platform.

3. How AstroHealth Works

AstroHealth follows an integrated workflow that transforms health information into understandable monitoring results and decision-support guidance.

The system brings together three main sources of information:

  • Wearable-Style Readings: Simulated time-series health readings representing data that could be collected from wearable devices.
  • Manual Health Check-ins: Daily health information and observations entered by the astronaut.
  • Photo-Based Assessments: Images submitted for experimental skin and wound-related analysis.

The collected information is processed by the platform's monitoring and analysis services, then presented through a unified dashboard.

Based on the available information, users can view health status indicators, follow trends, identify unusual heart-rate patterns, access emergency protocols, and retrieve relevant medical information through the AI-powered assistant.

The system combines rule-based logic, statistical analysis, and machine learning rather than depending on a single AI model for every function.

4. Health Monitoring & Interactive Dashboard

The AstroHealth dashboard provides a centralized view of astronaut health information, making it easier to monitor multiple indicators in one place.

It combines wearable-style readings and manual health check-ins to present health information in an organized and accessible format.

The platform uses predefined threshold-based rules to classify health readings into three status levels:

  • Green: The reading is within the configured normal range.
  • Yellow: The reading requires attention or monitoring.
  • Red: The reading has reached a configured alert threshold.

These classifications are generated through transparent rule-based logic, not by an AI model.

The dashboard also presents health trends and monitoring results to help users understand changes over time and identify readings that may require further attention.


5. AI, Trend Forecasting & Anomaly Detection

AstroHealth integrates machine learning and statistical analysis to provide additional insights into health data.

Heart-Rate Anomaly Detection

An LSTM Autoencoder model analyzes heart-rate time-series data to learn recurring patterns and identify observations that differ from the learned patterns.

Instead of relying only on fixed thresholds, this approach focuses on unusual patterns in the heart-rate data that may deserve further attention.

Health Trend Forecasting

The platform uses Linear Regression as its default forecasting method to estimate short-term trends in health indicators. It also includes an optional Chronos-based forecasting integration, which is disabled by default.

Statistical Monitoring

For health indicators other than heart rate, the platform applies statistical checks to highlight unusual readings.

Together, these components complement the rule-based monitoring system by providing trend information and additional signals for identifying potentially unusual health patterns.

These outputs are intended for screening and decision support, not medical diagnosis.

6. Emergency Assistance & Offline Protocols

During a space mission, access to immediate medical assistance may be limited. AstroHealth addresses this challenge through a collection of 11 predefined emergency decision-tree protocols.

These protocols provide structured, step-by-step guidance for different emergency scenarios.

Users can follow the decision paths to access relevant instructions based on the situation. The protocols are designed to operate fully offline, allowing astronauts to access predefined guidance even when an internet connection is unavailable.

This feature aims to make emergency instructions accessible and organized when timely support is essential.

The protocols provide informational guidance and do not replace professional medical care or mission-specific medical procedures.

7. AI-Powered Medical Assistant (RAG)

AstroHealth includes an AI-powered medical assistant built using a Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) approach.

The assistant retrieves relevant information from a collection of NASA human-spaceflight and medical resources before generating a response to the user's question.

The retrieval system combines:

  • Semantic Search: Uses the BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5 embedding model to retrieve passages based on their meaning.
  • BM25 Keyword Retrieval: Helps identify relevant passages using keyword matching.
  • Context-Based Generation: Uses the retrieved passages as context for generating an answer.

The assistant displays source references alongside its responses, allowing users to trace the information back to the retrieved material.

This approach helps connect AI-generated responses to relevant reference material instead of relying only on the language model's internal knowledge.

The assistant is designed to provide informational support and does not replace professional medical judgment.


8. Photo-Based Skin & Wound Assessment

AstroHealth includes an experimental photo-based assessment feature that allows users to submit images for skin and wound-related analysis.

The feature combines a vision-language model with an offline MobileNetV2 image classifier to analyze submitted images.

This adds a visual assessment component to the platform alongside its numerical health-monitoring capabilities.

The feature is intended as an experimental prototype for informational support. Its results are not medical diagnoses, and the component has not been validated as a medical-grade diagnostic system.

9. Technologies & System Architecture

AstroHealth is developed using a modular web architecture that combines frontend, backend, data processing, and AI components.

Backend Development

  • Python
  • FastAPI
  • Pydantic
  • SQLAlchemy
  • SQLite

Frontend Development

  • React
  • Vite
  • Recharts
  • Three.js

Machine Learning & AI

  • PyTorch
  • LSTM Autoencoder
  • Linear Regression
  • Optional Chronos integration
  • ONNX Runtime
  • MobileNetV2
  • OpenAI-compatible language and vision model endpoint

Retrieval-Augmented Generation

  • ChromaDB
  • Sentence Transformers
  • BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5
  • BM25

Development & Deployment

  • Docker
  • GitHub

The modular architecture allows the platform's monitoring, forecasting, anomaly detection, emergency assistance, and retrieval components to work together while maintaining separate responsibilities.

10. Expected Impact & Limitations

AstroHealth aims to support astronaut health monitoring and decision-making during long-duration space missions by bringing multiple capabilities into one accessible platform.

Its main contributions include:

  • Centralized Health Monitoring: Bringing different health indicators and daily check-ins into one dashboard.
  • Early Awareness: Highlighting unusual heart-rate patterns and health trends that may require attention.
  • Accessible Emergency Guidance: Providing 11 predefined emergency protocols that remain accessible offline.
  • NASA-Based Information Retrieval: Helping users access relevant information from NASA human-spaceflight resources through a source-referenced AI assistant.
  • Integrated Visual Assessment: Exploring photo-based analysis as an additional source of health information.

Prototype Limitations

AstroHealth is a working prototype and is not a certified medical device or diagnostic system.

Wearable-style readings used in the prototype are simulated rather than collected from astronauts in actual space missions. AI-based outputs and photo assessments are experimental and require further validation before any real-world medical use.

The platform is intended to demonstrate how monitoring, data analysis, machine learning, and information retrieval can be combined to support astronaut health awareness and decision-making.
